- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off or volatility anticipation.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% from prior high); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% of the spike magnitude.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to catch reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in early cycles (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “sentiment-weighted lag” correction: add 0.3–0.7% for each day of negative sentiment in prior 7 days.
